import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set style
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 10))

# Create subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(16, 12))

# 1. Price distribution by sensor type (boxplot)
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='sensor_type', y='price_usd', ax=axes[0, 0], palette='viridis')
axes[0, 0].set_title('Camera Price Distribution by Sensor Type', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Sensor Type', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 2. Megapixels vs Price colored by video capability (scatter plot)
video_colors = {0: '#FF6B6B', 1: '#4ECDC4'}
scatter = axes[0, 1].scatter(df['megapixels'], df['price_usd'], 
                            c=df['has_video_4k'].map(video_colors),
                            alpha=0.6, s=50, edgecolors='w', linewidth=0.5)
axes[0, 1].set_title('Megapixels vs Price by 4K Video Capability', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 1].set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)

# Create custom legend for video capability
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
legend_elements = [Line2D([0], [0], marker='o', color='w', markerfacecolor='#FF6B6B', 
                         markersize=10, label='No 4K Video'),
                   Line2D([0], [0], marker='o', color='w', markerfacecolor='#4ECDC4', 
                         markersize=10, label='Has 4K Video')]
axes[0, 1].legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='upper left')

# 3. Camera count by brand (top 10 brands)
top_brands = df['brand'].value_counts().head(10)
bars = axes[1, 0].barh(top_brands.index, top_brands.values, color=plt.cm.Set3(np.arange(10)/10))
axes[1, 0].set_title('Top 10 Camera Brands by Count', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('Number of Cameras', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Brand', fontsize=12)

# Add value labels on bars
for i, bar in enumerate(bars):
    width = bar.get_width()
    axes[1, 0].text(width + 1, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2, 
                   str(int(width)), va='center', fontsize=10)

# 4. Weight vs Price by body type (scatter with regression)
sns.scatterplot(data=df, x='weight_grams', y='price_usd', hue='body_type', 
                ax=axes[1, 1], alpha=0.7, s=60, palette='tab10')
sns.regplot(data=df, x='weight_grams', y='price_usd', 
           scatter=False, ax=axes[1, 1], color='gray', line_kws={'alpha': 0.5})
axes[1, 1].set_title('Weight vs Price by Body Type', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Weight (grams)', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].legend(title='Body Type', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Adjust layout
plt.suptitle('Digital Camera Market Analysis', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
plt.close()
